item.title: Taylor Swift donated 6,000 books to a library in 2011, helping it serve 27,452 people in 2025
item.description: In 2011, Taylor Swift generously donated 6,000 books to bolster local libraries in Berks County amid looming budget cuts. This pivotal support allowed the Reading Public Library to enrich its programs and attract thousands of community members. By 2025, the library circulated over 182,000 items and continued to foster engagement through various initiatives, proving Swift’s contribution remains vital for the region's library services to this day.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kansas couple transforms backyard into a 100,000-gallon tropical lagoon with six waterfalls
item.description: Melissa and Mike Morris dedicated nearly a year to constructing a stunning 100,000-gallon swimming lagoon in Olathe, Kansas. Inspired by the beauty of Tahiti, they created a coastal paradise at home, complete with granite rocks, flowing waterfalls, and vibrant tropical fish. Their captivating project drew attention online, leading to requests for exclusive photo sessions and events, while they relish their private backyard oasis as they finalize the landscaping.

item.title: Mahomes and Kelce’s jerseys sold for $250,000, helping raise $3.97 million for childhood cancer
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs stars, Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, showcased their commitment to charity by donating signed jerseys that sold for a remarkable $250,000. This generous contribution is part of the Big Slick Celebrity Weekend, which successfully raised $3.97 million for pediatric cancer initiatives at Children's Mercy Hospital, bringing total donations to over $21 million since the event's launch in 2010.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Yemen claims over 700 Houthis killed after 1,250 strikes rained within 24 hours
item.description: Yemen armed forces reported conducting 1,250 targeting operations against Houthis in one day. These strikes coincided with Houthi attacks on Aden’s presidential palace, resulting in casualties. Houthi spokesperson denied claims of missile strikes towards Medina, asserting their innocence. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition intercepted several missiles aimed at its territories amid ongoing tensions. Overall, hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia have intensified over recent months.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Indiana teen brothers, 15 and 14, rescue grandmother and two children from pond; toddler revived
item.description: During a tense moment in Carmel, Indiana, two brothers displayed extraordinary bravery by rescuing a grandmother and her grandchildren from a pond. Their ordeal began when a pushchair slipped into the water, triggering panic. The older brother dove in, employing life-saving measures that successfully revived a two-year-old boy who had momentarily lost consciousness. The brothers will receive community recognition for their courageous actions at the next city council meeting.

item.title: Thrift Find Becomes Windfall: £20 charity-shop jars confirmed as Qing porcelain; auction brings £58,000
item.description: A casual ceramics collector stumbled upon two seemingly ordinary porcelain jars in a London charity shop priced at just $25. After a detailed assessment, experts revealed these jars were actually rare 18th-century Qing Dynasty artifacts adorned with imperial designs and intricate floral patterns. The jars sparked considerable interest and fetched an astonishing £58,000 at auction, translating to over $74,000, significantly benefiting the charity involved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s Palm Beach mansion rises from $725,000 to $36 million
item.description: El Solano, a captivating mansion nestled in Palm Beach, was acquired by music legend John Lennon and his partner Yoko Ono in 1980. Following Lennon’s untimely passing, Yoko executed extensive renovations before offloading the property in 1986. The illustrious estate changed hands several times, skyrocketing in value, and ultimately fetched $36 million in 2020. Today, it stands as a cherished landmark, intertwining Lennon’s artistic legacy with architectural history.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Shark tours make people 40% more likely to protect sharks
item.description: Shark populations are declining significantly due to human activities and a third of species are threatened. Participation in shark ecotourism leads to increased conservation efforts among tourists and the public. After two years, those who engaged in ecotourism showed a 40% increase in conservation activities. Educational experiences during these tours provide vital information about the role of sharks in the ecosystem.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 28-foot statue of biblical pharaoh who enslaved Israelis discovered by Egyptian farmer
item.description: A farmer in Behbeit El Hagar, Egypt stumbled upon a remarkable royal statue of Ramses II while tilling his land. In a swift response, local antiquities officials began an excavation to retrieve the statue along with other artifacts. They uncovered a substantial head of Ramses II and several smaller statues embellished with inscriptions. This discovery is expected to deepen our knowledge of ancient Egypt's cultural and political legacy.

item.title: China, Pakistan hold high-altitude army drills with Beijing-supplied arms
item.description: In a landmark move, China and Pakistan have kicked off their inaugural joint military exercise, dubbed Karakoram 2026, in the high-altitude region of Xinjiang. This operation emphasizes counter-terrorism strategies, utilizing advanced Chinese military technology. The participating forces aim to refine their skills in mountainous terrains, thus fortifying the strategic partnership between the two nations. The exercise promises improved synergy as troops navigate shared operational standards.
